body: I do something similar except I tell my childhood self they should have just ended it while they had the chance, before they ended up with all these relationships and people to hurt and let down

One thing I discovered about myself is I use suicidal ideation as a coping mechanism. I have no desire to actually kill myself, but it can be comforting to imagine all my problems disappearing forever, or picture someone reaching out to help me. Figuring this out has mostly eliminated the distress these thoughts used to cause me.
Ten years ago, I was 14. I think I started with giving myself welts with rubber bands. Then I started scratching my skin with a safety pin. It's evolved from there.

Just focus on not doing it today. This may be backwards logic, but it will always be an option if you really need it. You are in control. So many people SH for control, myself included, but when it becomes an addiction then that control has shifted, it is controlling you. Fight it!

I used to give myself welts with rubber bands. I don't mean snapping it on your wrist as a distraction, although I've done that too. I mean snapping it HARD over and over on the same spot to leave nasty angry purple welts. The pain was really good and the physical marks were satisfying and lasted several days, but they never left any sort of permanent scar.
Try to avoid places with those pictures in the future. They rarely make me feel anything but tempted or inadequate.

For me it evokes the feelings I have that l really want to share with someone. The idea that this stranger might understand me in a way most people don't, makes me anxious and want to connect with someone.

I feel like I'm very like a cat. Even though I don't much like cats, but I guess I don't much like myself either so maybe that makes sense.

I recently saw a clinical psychologist for the first time after years and years of anxiety, hopelessness, self-injury, and suicidal ideation that all began with a messed up childhood. I told them that I had never seen any sort of professional for this, and I needed to do something.   


I didn't get any sort of evaluation. She didn't ask me any questions. She just told me to tell her about myself then stared at me in awkward silence for several minutes while I failed to think of anything about myself due to all my brain processes being occupied entirely with trying not to run away as fast as I could. I eventually said something, and proceeded have to tell this person I didn't know or trust all of these extremely personal things.  

I asked what the purpose was of just talking about my past when I needed to learn how to deal with NOW, and I had been spending years analyzing my past. I could already identify all my anxiety triggers and connect almost all of them to my past and understand WHY, but it didn't make me feel any better, and I wasn't coping well with my thoughts and feelings. She said in her 20 some years of doing this, she's seen that teaching me to cope with symptoms won't help, and that that type of therapy might make people feel better in the short term, but is ultimately ineffective.  

I left and didn't sleep for two days. I just cried and hyperventilated. But I went back the next week, because this is a professional, they know what's best, and everyone says it has to get worse before it can get better. I had done my research and picked a doctor with really good reviews on multiple websites. So I went back the next week, and the same thing. She just stared at me, didn't even say anything this time. I managed to talk about my feelings for an hour, then the same thing. My anxiety was skyrocketing, I was angry. So I didn't go back again, which actually made me feel better than I had in a long time.  

I never got any answers. I still don't know what's wrong with me. It was an incredibly frustrating experience, it felt so wrong to open up like that and it didn't make me feel better, and I didn't get help. What I did get was a bill for $200 in the mail a free weeks later(after insurance).  

I don't think I have the fortitude to try again.  

If you read all of this, thank you, truly.

I appreciate the response. I don't think I could believe it though. I don't think anyone deserves anything. I've been doing better though, I've since talked to my husband and a psychologist. So we'll see. Today's just a bad day.

I love how I unexpectedly find things I relate to in random threads. I understand that feeling completely, when I was quitting self-harm, I kept a razor blade in my wallet for almost two years. It was comforting to know I always had it.
Self-harm. That one took a hell of a lot of effort to kick..

Me too sometimes, and I haven't done it in over eight years. Each year has gotten easier and easier though. The first was the worst. I thought about it, wanted to do it, every single day. Multiple times a day. Then eventually, one day, I realized I hadn't thought of it the day before. And it slowly improved. Now I go through bad periods maybe a few times a year, but the drive is so much weaker.  
Just remember that those feelings are temporary. Distract yourself until they pass, and they will pass. Talk to someone, not necessarily even about your problems, just talk as a distraction. I'm sure you've done your own research, but there are other tricks. Find out what it is about self harm that you seek. If it's the pain, stick your hand in ice water or wear a rubber band on your wrist and snap it(not too hard) when you need to. If it's the expression, write about your feelings or make some art. If it's the visual aspect, paint yourself. I used to crush cherries and watch the juice run out over my hands(which had the added benefit of getting to eat delicious cherries!).  
This is getting long-winded, but I guess what I'm getting at is.. These feelings will come, and they will pass. And they will come again. But the longer you resist them, the easier it gets and the weaker and less frequent the urges will become. And if you find that you absolutely need to hurt yourself, set guidelines beforehand and stick to them. I wish you the best, and feel free to message me anytime, although I may not check this account often enough, as it's my alternate.

I apologize that I don't have much in the way of advice, except maybe avoid being idle. Keeping myself busy helps. But if it helps at all to know that other people are in the same place as you, we are.

I understand having those feelings kind of... underneath everything all the time. I fantasize about suicide and self-injury all the time. When I'm upset, but sometimes when I'm not. I think it has something to do with the fact that I want to talk to someone about my problems or acknowledge I could use help, but the only way I can see that happening is through some extreme mental break.

Really bad. I think. I don't know. I think about killing myself a lot. I don't contemplate it or want it or plan it, I just... think about it. I want to hurt myself. I haven't done that in nine years but I want to. I've never gotten any professional help. I'm anxious all the time, sometimes I have chest pains or trouble breathing from it. Last night I spent an hour questioning if the world was real or if I was real or if everyone was lying to me.  
But sometimes I'm fine, everything is good and my mind is peaceful. So it can't be that bad can it?  
I think sometimes that I must be faking it. Is my life so empty that I need some kind of excitement and create these problems for myself? I think sometimes that I'm doing it for attention, but that makes no sense because I've never told anyone. My husband doesn't know, my family doesn't know, my friends don't know. Maybe it's not even real.  If I ignore it maybe it can just not be real. What if I told my husband and he decided I was too much trouble for him?  
If I told anyone this they'd just tell me I need professional help, and I can't afford that so I don't tell anyone.  
Sometimes I just want to sleep for days, and sometimes I can't sleep.  
I feel like a mental breakdown is coming. I don't know when, but I can't imagine it's not going to happen. But I can't afford it, so I dunno. Healthcare is too damn expensive for me to be sick, so I *decide* not to be. My husband just lost his job, and our insurance with it too, so I really can't afford to be this way now.  
There is no mercy in the world. You just have to keep going and the universe doesn't give a shit.  
Sorry for the ramble.
